reasoning_chain: The question has three parts: a deadline for concluding the human review, the procedure that governs it, and the regulator the subscriber can turn to if it does not happen.

[pdpl-45-2021-en:18(4)] says only that the Controller must include the human element in reviewing automated processing decisions when the Data Subject asks. It sets no time limit, describes no review procedure, and names no regulator or complaint route.
[pdpl-45-2021-en:18(2)] lists the cases in which the Data Subject may not object to automated decisions. It does not address the timing, procedure or escalation of a human review.

[pdpl-45-2021-en:6(1)] covers consent requirements. [pdpl-45-2021-en:7(5)] and [pdpl-45-2021-en:8(1)] cover Processor appointment and the Processor's instructions. [pdpl-45-2021-en:23(2)] covers cross-border transfer. None of them sets a review deadline, a procedure or a supervisory authority.

[tdra-cpr-v2-en:4.17.3] is about voice-recording verbal consent to terms and conditions. [cabinet-66-2023-en:34(3)] is about providers deciding conformity by themselves. Neither concerns human review of automated decisions or a route for complaints.

No clause supplied answers any of the three parts, so I am proposing nothing. A deadline, a procedure and a competent authority would each need to come from clauses not provided here, such as the PDPL Executive Regulations or a complaints provision. I have not seen those and cannot cite them.
